liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (4 reviews): Reviewer praises the great Shakedown jam; Shakedown runs well over fifteen minutes; reviewer rates it among the best ever performed [14][15][20][21]
- **Dark Star Tease** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Bruce teases Dark Star repeatedly before Drums, but Jerry starts a different song at each break; Reviewer singles out the Dark Star teaser as a real treat [3][11][14][16]
- **Hell in a Bucket** (1 review): Reviewer says the show is a smoker from the moment Bucket starts [15]
- **Foolish Heart** (1 review): Reviewer calls Foolish Heart spectacular and says Jerry's solo in it still brings a big grin [10]
- **Jam** (1 review): Reviewer lists the bubble jam after Terrapin as a highlight [10]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer names Black Peter among the highlights, alongside the Dark Star jam [10]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): After Space, Jerry leads the band into Dark Star [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-06-22.179539.senn.me88.braund.andrewf.flac2448** (recommended): source not stated; 21 songs; 185 min [1]. Said about its sound: Notes say there is no wind-rumble noise on the Playing In The Band Reprise [1]
- **gd1991-06-22.sbd.unknown.29057.sbe-fix.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 176 min; rated 4.38/5 by 37 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the sound at the show was great and this soundboard is too [20]
- **gd1991-06-22.150678.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 181 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [4]
- **gd1991-06-22.sbd.miller.105541.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 179 min; rated 4.5/5 by 6 [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says Hornsby pushed Garcia to play beyond his usual self during this show [11]
- Stadium set off fireworks around its outer rim after the show, which the audience did not expect [13]
- Chicago's Sears Tower was visible inside the stadium behind the band [13]
- Roger McGuinn opened the show [13]
- Roger McGuinn played the warm-up set, which the reviewer found killer [14]
- Reviewer's first show; recalls a fan wiggling to Hey Mr. Spaceman nearby [16]
- Reviewer walked up from under McCormick Plaza into a sea of tie-dyes and VW buses, and was welcomed [18]
- Wind blew toward the stadium's south end, whipping Garcia's long hair back during the Foolish Heart jam [20]
- Reviewer finds the second set very similar to the equally good Vegas and Shoreline shows [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-06-22.179539.senn.me88.braund.andrewf.flac2448**: taped by Steve Braund; transferred by Andrew F; source: Sennheiser ME-88's (unknown mic power/body, likely K3) > Sony TC-D5M (Dolby Out) > Denon HD-8 [1]. Also: This recording is patched in places with other recordings, listed by ID, including crowd, Terrapin and Saturday Night patches [1]
- **gd1991-06-22.sbd.unknown.29057.sbe-fix.flac16**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: A few pops on disc two were fixed; the notes refer to separate declicking information [2]
- **gd1991-06-22.150678.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  October 2, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [4]. Also: Tape flips and some tuning were patched using a master DAT soundboard [4]
- **gd1991-06-22.sbd.miller.105541.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Dat -> Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1991-06-22 Sat Soldier Field, Chicago, IL](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1274988387729/grateful-dead-1991-06-22-sat-soldier) [26]
